conviction.explanation: 21% operating-income and 22% adjusted-EPS growth, rising CFO and $66.987bn annual cash FCF support funded compounding at 30.63x adjusted FY earnings. Falling FCF, capital intensity and overbought extension constrain the positive conviction despite strong funding.

executive_summary:
Microsoft supports patient ownership through funded operating growth: FY operating income rose 21% and adjusted EPS 22%, while CFO increased to $182.935bn. Annual cash FCF remained $66.987bn after $115.948bn cash PP&E, with liquid assets exceeding stated debt by $36.549bn before leases.

The 30.63x OpenAI-adjusted FY multiple requires durable compounding. Capex nearly doubled and FCF fell 6.5%, while noncash equipment and lease burdens sit beyond the cash measure. Azure growth is substantive demand evidence, but overbought price extension and declining cloud gross margin argue for deliberate additions.
bull_case: Growing profitable cloud activity and strong internal funding can earn the premium while continuing investment and shareholder returns.
bear_case: Infrastructure costs can outpace incremental returns, weakening owner cash and compressing the multiple even while earnings grow.
key_uncertainties: Returns on incremental cloud capacity and future capital intensity.
Full lease and noncash-equipment commitments beyond cash-PP&E FCF.
Persistence of adjusted earnings growth at the current valuation.
catalysts_upcoming: Next cloud results: sustained operating growth with improved gross-margin or cash conversion would strengthen the thesis.
Comparable cash-flow and lease disclosures showing investment demands stabilize relative to CFO would support owner returns.

correlation_notes: Sector: Technology — use sector-specific catalysts and risks in the thesis.
risk_assessment.max_drawdown_scenario: Historical max drawdown: 37.1% over available price history. Projected worst case (2-sigma): ~79.7% from current $529.30.

action_plan.target_rationale: TP1 = nearest technical resistance (SMA-200, BB-upper, or 52w high). TP2 = 52w high / +15% stretch. Consider scaling out: sell half at TP1, let the rest ride to TP2.

research_verdict.thesis: Microsoft supports a funded-compounding purchase: operating income grew 21%, adjusted EPS 22%, and annual cash FCF remained $66.987bn despite nearly doubled capex. Rising CFO and a $36.549bn liquid surplus excluding leases give the bull measured financing and growth support at 30.63x OpenAI-adjusted FY earnings. The 6.5% FCF decline and premium valuation constrain conviction, but imperfect conversion does not outweigh the large positive cash engine.
research_verdict.strongest_counterexample: Cash FCF declined while earnings grew, and its cash-PP&E definition excludes noncash equipment and some lease demands; poor incremental cloud returns could compress the premium despite accounting growth.
invalidation_conditions: Next comparable annual cash FCF below $66.987bn alongside no year-on-year operating-income growth would undermine the funded-compounding basis.
A comparable year with cash PP&E exceeding CFO, from $115.948bn versus $182.935bn, would invalidate the positive cash-funding foundation.
decisive_factors: CFO increased from $136.162bn to $182.935bn, establishing actual internal funding growth.
Adjusted EPS basis avoids investment-gain cheapness; technical extension argues for deliberate timing.
